questions.q: A senior software engineer has recently been assigned to manage a project using the Agile approach. To ensure that they successfully deliver the project, the project manager should first: *

o.t: Identify all risks
Determine all of the sprints’ activities
Define the project success criteria
Define quality metrics

questions.e: In Agile, it is essential to define success criteria from the beginning to ensure that the project meets stakeholder expectations.

questions.q: After 8 years of experience in the same position, a project manager gets promoted to a Portfolio manager role. A portfolio is: *

o.t: A number of projects, programs, or operations that are all managed as a collection with the aim to achieve the organization’s strategic goals
Analyzing IT requirements and ensuring regulatory requirements are followed.
Following methods, processes, and tools to ensure that projects are managed as designed.
Creates a common vision and helps senior management to see the potential strategic implications of corporate decisions.

questions.e: A portfolio is a collection of projects, programs, and operations managed together to achieve strategic objectives. This holistic management approach ensures that all initiatives align with the organization's goals and optimize resource use.

questions.q: You have recommended developing a business case for each of the organizational projects followed by the development of a project benefits management plan. Who would you recommend to be the owner of the business case ? *

o.t: Change Control Board.
Project team.
Project manager.
Project sponsor.

questions.e: The business case justifies the project and defines its business value. It is typically owned by the sponsor, who is responsible for funding.

questions.q: The traditional project management approaches place the project manager at the center of coordination for the project and makes them responsible for the project tracking and reporting. However, this approach is not suitable for : *

o.t: Low-change projects where detailed scope has been provided by the client organization.
Projects where detailed schedules are required to be developed and approved by the clients.
Projects that require front-loaded planning work.
High-change projects where there is more complexity than one person can manage.

questions.e: Traditional approaches work well for stable projects, whereas high-change projects require an Agile approach.

questions.q: A project has just been initiated to transform an organization from a functional organizational structure to Projectized. If the project is successful in meeting its objectives, what will be the most likely outcome ? (Choose three) : *

o.t: The role of the project manager(s) will be defined as a project coordinator.
The organization will shift from the current state to the desired future state.
The project manager(s) will have control over the project budget.
The project manager(s) will have significantly more authority over projects.
Employees will be grouped by the work being done (engineering, manufacturing, etc.)

questions.e: In a projectized organization, project managers have more authority and control over budgeting.

questions.q: In order to ensure that the project is performed in accordance with the organization’s requirements, the project manager carries out a tailoring process. Under this context, Tailoring is: *

o.t: The knowledge and practices which are applicable to most projects in most cases
The application of a set of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to the project activities in order to meet its requirements
The selection of the appropriate processes, inputs, tools, techniques, and life cycle phases for managing a project
The application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques needed for meeting a program's requirements

questions.e: Tailoring involves adapting methodologies and tools to meet the specific needs of the project.

questions.q: A project manager acquired information from the market that would reduce the business value being delivered by an ongoing project. Based on that information, the project manager believes the project should be stopped. How should the project manager handle the situation ? *

o.t: Have a discussion with the project sponsor and cancel the project.
Have a discussion with the sponsor and recommend the project business value be reassessed.
Continue working on the defined scope and review the risk matrix.
Remove the items no longer applicable from the backlog and present the backlog to the project team.

questions.e: Project termination must be justified and validated with the sponsor, who owns the business case.

questions.q: You are a project manager in a construction project. What should you do to ensure the successful delivery of the project ? *

o.t: Identify the project’s risks and necessary success criteria.
Meet with stakeholders to communicate the schedule budget, and cost impact in the event of a project delay.
Establish a management reserve to handle the unknown risks when occurs.
Conduct a team-building activity.

questions.e: Identifying risks and success criteria is critical to ensuring project success.

questions.q: A project manager is asked to contribute to a document to describe what is intended to be achieved with a project once it is successfully finished, and how this will be measured. What could be the name of that document ? *

o.t: Change management plan.
Statement of work.
Benefits management plan.
management plan.

questions.e: This document defines how the project's benefits will be realized and measured.

questions.q: You are working as a part-time manager at a weak matrix organization. Your functional manager adds to your workload by declaring you the project manager for a new business idea. After reviewing the business case, you understand new personnel will need to be hired to execute the project. What constraint, if any, will you be operating under in terms of hiring additional staff? *

o.t: All stakeholders would be responsible for hiring staff.
You, as project manager, would be responsible for hiring staff.
The functional manager would be responsible for hiring staff.
Senior management would be responsible for hiring staff.

questions.e: In a weak matrix, the functional manager retains authority over hiring and resource allocation.

questions.q: You are the Project Manager of a project in which team members have a dual reporting structure. In addition to reporting to you, they also report to their functional manager. Also, the team members are expected to do the project work along with department work. You are working in which form of organization ? *

o.t: Tight Matrix.
Functional.
Matrix.
Projected.

questions.e: A matrix organization combines project teams and functional managers, resulting in a dual reporting structure.

questions.q: Which of the following business documents Justify why the project is authorized ? *

o.t: Project management plan.
Business case
Project charter.
Scope statement of work.

questions.e: The business case justifies why the project exists by outlining its benefits and business value.

questions.q: What is the difference between a predictive lifecycle and an adaptive lifecycle ? *

o.t: Predictive lifecycle forecasts project completion ; adaptive lifecycle completes the project when the money runs out.
Predictive lifecycle is plan-driven ; adaptive lifecycle is change-driven.
There is no difference.
The predictive follows the same pattern for each iteration and the adaptive lifecycle changes its approach based upon performance growth of the project results.

questions.e: Predictive (Waterfall) = follows a detailed plan Adaptive (Agile) = flexibility to accommodate changes

questions.q: In addition to the departments listed in the scenario, your company also has a manager of project management to oversee all of the ongoing projects. As one of the project managers, you report directly to the project management department but share staff with other departments. What type of organizational structure does this describe ? *

o.t: Composite.
Functional.
Matrix.
Projected.

questions.e: In a matrix structure, resources are shared between multiple departments.

questions.q: Early in the establishment of the project, the project manager spends time looking for historical data that might be helpful in planning the new project. She is looking for examples of project documents in similar projects that have been completed that she might be able to use as templates for the new project. She is also looking for information about established processes and procedures that will help the project run more smoothly. What is the term used to define these ? *

o.t: Organizational process assets (OPAS).
Enterprise environmental factors (EEFS).
Retrospective.
Progressive elaboration.

questions.e: OPAs include templates, historical project documents, and organizational processes.

questions.q: A skilled project manager should have the necessary expertise to identify appropriate project management approaches (traditional vs. Agile) and tailor the tools, techniques, and methods for each project. What are these skills called ? *

o.t: Strategic and business management skills.
Leadership skills.
Technical project management skills.
Interpersonal skills.

questions.e: A competent project manager must adapt tools and methodologies based on the project's context.

questions.q: In a weak matrix organization, employees work across multiple projects and with various departments within the company to increase employee interaction and promote teamwork spirit. In the event that additional employees are needed, who is in charge of the hiring process under this matrix? *

o.t: The project manager
The sponsor
The project team
The functional manager

questions.e: In a weak matrix, the functional manager controls hiring and resource management.

questions.q: Which of the following is the top priority for an agile project? *

o.t: Working collaboratively with customer and having a lightweight contract.
Satisfying the customer through delivery of valuable product.
Providing working software and accurate documentation.
Responding to change and following adaptive plan.

questions.e: The Agile Manifesto prioritizes customer satisfaction through continuous and rapid delivery.

questions.q: What could be a PMO role in agile transformation? *

o.t: Providing guidelines to ensure compliance with agile frameworks.
Providing agile tools like Kanban boards and burn charts.
Providing project managers to new agile projects.
Ensuring compliance with standard team velocity.

questions.e: An Agile PMO helps align Agile practices with the organization's governance requirements.

questions.q: There are over 40 stakeholders on a new Java training project, and no one can agree on project objectives. One stakeholder believes the project can achieve a 30% improvement in team's knowledge of Java while another believes a 40% improvement is possible. The project manager believes a 20% improvement is more realistic. What is the best course of action? *

o.t: Perform feasibility analysis
Use the average of these numbers
Ask the sponsor to make the final decision
Use your decision as you are the project manager

questions.e: A feasibility analysis helps determine realistic objectives based on concrete data.

questions.q: A project manager has been assigned to an existing agile team and is preparing for an upcoming project. The last project that the team worked on was so successful that a senior stakeholder requested that the team use the same governance structure for the new project. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Consult with the project management office (PMO) to gain their insight on governance for the project.
Collaborate with the team and the senior stakeholder to discuss tailoring the existing governance.
Inform senior management that the same project governance can be used for the new project.
Request that the senior stakeholder discuss all governance-related concerns with the product owner.

questions.e: The project manager should collaborate with the project team and the senior stakeholder to tailor the existing governance to the new project. While the previous governance structure was successful, tailoring ensures it aligns with the specific needs of the current project. Simply using the same structure without review may not be effective.

questions.q: The government of a country intends to construct a multibillion-dollar railway across three major cities and hires a contractor to oversee construction. The project’s design will be finalized within a few months, but the government has time constraints and expects the project to be completed within 24 months. The project manager wants to ensure a balanced distribution of risk between the government and the contractor. Which two techniques should be considered during the development of the project management plan? (Choose two) *

o.t: Fixed-price increments
Not-to-exceed time
Early cancellation option
Dynamic scope option
Graduated time and materials

questions.e: Fixed-price increments ensure payments are made after completing specific project phases, which reduces financial risk for both parties. Graduated time and materials ensure costs are adjusted based on project progress, which helps distribute risk between the government and the contractor.

questions.q: A project manager has just received news that a new regulation has been adopted, and the project must now comply with it. Previously, this was documented as a risk item with a low probability and moderate impact. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Revisit the risk register and update the rating and response.
Update the issue log and apply corrective action.
Revise the project management plan.
Initiate a change request for the updated regulation.

questions.e: Since the regulation has been officially adopted, the probability of this risk has changed to 100%. The project manager should update the risk register before taking further action. This ensures that the team properly assesses the impact before modifying the project management plan or initiating change requests.

questions.q: Although a project is performing within its time, scope, and budget constraints, the project manager learns that the project sponsor is unhappy with its progress. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Conducted frequent reviews and assessments to identify and address any potential risks.
Aligned project objectives with the expectations and requirements of the project sponsor.
Communicated regularly with the project sponsor to provide updates and address any concerns.
Implemented strict control measures to ensure that project milestones and deliverables are met.

questions.e: Even if the project is meeting scope, schedule, and budget goals, stakeholders may still be dissatisfied if their expectations are not managed properly. Regular communication with the sponsor ensures that concerns are addressed before they escalate.

questions.q: A project manager is beginning a new financial software project in a highly competitive environment. The regulations for compliance are clear, but the requirements are not well-defined. The customer stresses that they need results as soon as possible. Which implementation approach should the project manager choose for this project? *

o.t: Repeating and refining project phases in multiple iterations.
Progressing through a linear sequence of stages.
Embracing change and focusing on delivering value.
Focusing on delivering the project in multiple increments.

questions.e: Incremental delivery allows the team to deliver value quickly while refining requirements based on feedback. Since compliance regulations are clear, the team can ensure regulatory alignment while adapting to changing customer needs.
